facility.name: Lionheart Childrens Academy
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Before School Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Drop-In Care,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name: Cots in four of the classrooms were not labeled.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Cots, Beds, Mats Labeled With Child's Name (26 TAC §746.4503(b))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: Infant feeding sheets in two infant rooms were not updated.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months: According to documentation the operations fire inspection was conduced on 2/26/2025 and the operation stated that had an isnpection completed but did not have the report avaliable for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Fire Inspection - Before Initial Permit Issued and Every 12 Months (26 TAC §746.5101(a))

occurrences.finding: Report Change in Director: The operation made a change in Director on 3/2/2026 and did not notify licensing.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Change in Director (26 TAC §746.303(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Complying with Laws and Rules: The governing body failed to implement plans that will prevent prohibited discipline issues at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Complying with Laws and Rules (26 TAC §746.201(9))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment: A caregiver was observed popping a child on the hand and on the back of the head.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Corporal Punishment (26 TAC §746.2805(1))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A toddler was left unsupervised for three minutes on the playground.  The caregiver realized that the child was missing when they returned to the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and found to be deficient.  The caregiver inappropriately grabbed and pulled a child while in care at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Caregivers Have Access to Tracking System: The caregiver failed to use the tracking system appropriately.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Caregivers Have Access to Tracking System (26 TAC §746.631(b))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A two year old child was left unattended outside of their classroom for five minutes.  The child was found by a caregiver.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A staff member failed to supervise the children appropriately in the classroom.  Two staff members were talking to one another through a door which resulted in an incident occurring in the classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A toddler was left unsupervised for two minutes inside the building.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training: A caregiver was observed pulling a child towards them and tapping them on their head. The incident happened during naptime and the child was lying on their cot.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments -  Associated with Food, Naps, or Toilet Training (26 TAC §746.2805(2))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A toddler was left unsupervised for thirteen minutes in a classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers: A caregiver failed to communicate with a teacher that she was bringing a child to their classroom.  The caregiver opened the door and the child entered without a teacher in place.  The toddler was alone in the classroom for thirteen minutes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Share Information with Incoming Caregivers (26 TAC §746.1203(10))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A four year old was left unsupervised when their class went outside to the playground.  The child was left for one minute and was found by the director in the building by the back door.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information-Completed Food Allergy Plan: One allergy plan evaluated did not have the parent's signature.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information-Completed Food Allergy Plan (26 TAC §746.605(16))

occurrences.finding: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: Two children's records evaluated did not have current immunizations on file.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Immunization Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §746.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: A staff member was viewed on camera pulling a child up by the arms and dragging them a short distance to get them to stay in the designated area.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity: A staff member failed to supervise children appropriately on the playground.  A staff member was unaware that children were in a blind spot on the playground which resulted in them opening and closing the gate.  The children were observed walking out of the gate.  The children were observed using the playground equipment inappropriately.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A staff member failed to use good judgment when she allowed a parent to assist her in carrying a child into the operation.  The staff member was not prepared for an emergency due to not having a working walkie talkie and FOB to open the door.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Minimum Standards: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and it was determined that a caregiver witnessed another caregiver abusing children and did not report it to Child Care Regulation or notify the director.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Minimum Standards (26 TAC §746.1203(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and it was determined that a caregiver was pulling and grabbing children inappropriately to get them to lie down on their nap mats.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Grabbing and Pulling (26 TAC §746.2805(3))

occurrences.finding: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited: This standard was evaluated as part of an investigation and was determined that a caregiver was being rough with children.  The caregiver was seen on video grabbing and pulling children, forcefully putting them on their nap mats, pushing a child's face into the mat and picking children up by their forearms and carrying them across the room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Ensure No Child Abused, Neglected, or Exploited (26 TAC §746.1201(4))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area: During an investigation it was determined that the caregiver failed to disinfect the changing table between diaper changes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Sanitizing Diaper Changing Area (26 TAC §746.3505(e))

occurrences.finding: Diapering Procedures - Wash Infant's Hands: During an investigation it was determined that the infants hands were not being washed after diaper changes.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Diapering Procedures - Wash Infant's Hands (26 TAC §746.3505(b))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A staff member was turning the toy shelves against the wall so the children would not have access to them.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device: A caregiver was observed exceeding the amount of time that a child is in time out.  One child was put in a high chair for time out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Using Inappropriate Long Period of Silence or Inactivity Including Requiring Child to Remain in a Restrictive Device (26 TAC §746.2805(10))

occurrences.finding: Prohibited Punishments - Hitting with Hand or Instrument: A caregiver was observed popping a child on the leg with their hand when they would not stay in time out.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Prohibited Punishments - Hitting with Hand or Instrument (26 TAC §746.2805(4))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A staff member picked up a child by the arms while transitioning to a diaper change.  The transition resulted in an injury of Nursemaid's Elbow.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages: A caregiver was feeding an infant a breast milk bottle when a coworker realized she had the wrong baby.  The caregiver had confused the two infants.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Know Children's Names and Ages (26 TAC §746.1203(3))
